properties.name: manhattan_1867
properties.map: Plan of New York City, from the Battery to Spuyten Duyvil Creek, showing every lot and building thereon — M. Dripps, New York 1867 (based on the surveys of Randel & Blackwell and J. F. Harrison), sheets 9-18 of 20
properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged

properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged

properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged

properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged

properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged

properties.map_url: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/510d47e2-49f3-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (sheet 9; the other sheets follow in the same NYPL item series)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points, one fit per sheet (maps 8575-8584; 3 to 5 points each, affine); cross-validated residual by sheet 0-27 m, median 8 m; sheet 12 sits about 25 m off today's streets by eye; a street-matching refinement found too few windows and was not applied
properties.note: The plan hatches every building and leaves empty lots as outlines. Built-up = hatched ground (darker than the local paper tone by 0.11 after a 10 m median), closed across streets (16 m), yards under 0.6 ha filled, groups under 0.5 ha dropped. Only sheets 9-18 were read: 20th St to the Harlem River, 3,432 ha; south of 20th St the polygon is the 1852 extent (the city there was solid). Central Park is cut out (its planting is drawn as dark as blocks). North of 59th St this is the first snapshot that reaches Yorkville, Bloomingdale, Manhattanville and Harlem: there the built pieces are villages and house rows, and rock hachures or stains may be read as built in places. Sheet edges: 25 m inside each neat line, so a strip along a sheet join can be missing.
properties.method: every sheet read by tone inside its Map Warper mask (tools/mosaic.py), the readings merged
